title: Add soft-delete and retention_until fields to the User model
description: In applications/db-models/repos/onfinance-db-model-master/onfinance_db_model_master/models.py, class User(Document) (lines 387-429): add is_active = BooleanField(default=True), deleted_at = DateTimeField(), consent_withdrawn_at = DateTimeField() and retention_until = DateTimeField(). Add meta = {"collection": "user", "indexes": ["retention_until"]} with the collection name pinned. Do not use a hard TTL on User, because statutory retention applies. Set retention_until = deleted_at or consent_withdrawn_at + the task 1 period, in the account-closure and consent-withdrawal paths. Deploy dev -> qa -> prod with a pre-deploy backup, and honour any changeFreeze in applications/db-models/env/*.json.
acceptanceCriteria: python -c "from onfinance_db_model_master.models import User; print(sorted(k for k in User._fields if k in ('is_active','deleted_at','consent_withdrawn_at','retention_until')))" prints all four field names
In qa, closing a test account sets deleted_at and a retention_until equal to deleted_at plus the scheduled period

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-schemas on db-models/onfinance-db-model-master after tasks 2 and 3 merge. Expected: no SCH-RET-02 result for onfinance_db_model_master/models.py, and the observation for sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S13 no longer reports a missing retention field for User or Secrets.

rootCause.description: The User model only has account_creation_date and integration timestamps; nobody designed a closure, consent-withdrawal or retention-end marker, so no record can ever be identified as due for erasure.
